title: How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay: Casual Loading, Super, and Salary Sacrifice Tax Explained
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary with casual loading and super. Understand salary sacrifice tax and the 38-hour week for Australian workers.
salarySummary: For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours a week, the annual gross pay is about $52,265 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my hourly to annual conversion?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. When converting to annual pay, you multiply the loaded rate by hours per week and 52 weeks. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 becomes $33.05 with casual loading. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains this further.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings, not included in the hourly rate. The current super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual gross is $52,265, your employer adds about $6,272 in super, making total remuneration $58,537. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for details.

faqs.q: What is salary sacrifice tax and how does it affect my take-home pay?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice tax refers to the tax treatment when you forego part of your salary in exchange for benefits like a car or extra super contributions. Sacrificed amounts are generally taxed at your marginal rate, but can reduce your taxable income. Our calculator does not deduct salary sacrifice arrangements; you should consult the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for personalised estimates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

Converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward: multiply your hourly pay by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time worker, we assume a 38-hour week as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives you the gross annual figure before tax, super, and any deductions.

### The 38-Hour Week and Fortnightly Pay

If you work 38 hours per week, your annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. That works out to $1,004.90 per week and $52,265.44 per year. Many employers pay fortnightly, so your gross fortnightly pay would be $2,009.80 (weekly × 2). This is a useful figure for budgeting.

It’s important to note that this calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If your hours vary, you’ll need to average them over a longer period. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more on the current rates.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. When using our timesheet, you can check a box to add casual loading. **Never type a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual gross is $52,265, your employer must contribute an extra $6,271.80 into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it’s additional remuneration. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) pages explain these concepts in detail.

### Salary Sacrifice Tax and Your Take-Home Pay

Salary sacrifice tax refers to the tax treatment when you agree to reduce your salary in exchange for benefits such as a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. The sacrificed amount is generally taxed at your marginal rate but can lower your taxable income, potentially reducing the tax you pay. However, salary sacrifice arrangements are not included in our simple hourly-to-annual conversion – you should consult a tax professional or use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more personalised estimate.

Our tax estimate uses the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Note that the Medicare levy reduction thresholds used are from 2025–26, as the 2026–27 figures were not confirmed at the time of preparation. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

### Important Distinctions and Limitations

- **National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates**: The minimum wage of $26.44 is the legal floor. Many awards and enterprise agreements set higher rates. Our calculator uses the rate you enter, not a job median. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page shows industry averages from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, but these are averages, not medians for your specific job.
- **Award Rates**: If you are covered by an award, your minimum pay may be higher than the National Minimum Wage. Check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.
- **Casual Loading**: As mentioned, casuals get 25% on top. Permanent employees do not receive this loading but get paid leave.
- **Super on Top**: Super is additional to your gross pay. It does not reduce your take-home pay.
- **Salary Sacrifice Tax**: Arrangements can affect your taxable income and therefore your tax. They are not reflected in this basic conversion.

For a full breakdown, refer to the [reference tables](/data) or the [about the timesheet](/about) page. Remember, this is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax liability.
